methodology.target: House adoption of at least one article and Senate conviction on at least one article by the stated deadline, including proceedings after departure.
methodology.limits: Subjective political estimates, not calibrated odds or criminal-guilt judgments. Cases are not independent. Watchlist entries have no estimate; they are not zero risk. Close rankings are uncertain.
methodology.arithmetic: Overall conviction equals House impeachment multiplied by conviction conditional on impeachment. Probabilities across people do not sum to 100%.
methodology.momentum_rule: Assess changes in the political cost and feasibility of later proceedings, including unrelated cases. Record normalization, exceptional-case and backlash explanations; update every affected case with evidence or an explicit hold. Never apply a fixed uplift or infer guilt from another official’s conviction.
methodology.departure_rule: Resignation or dismissal does not automatically preclude impeachment or trial. Consider continuing accountability and disqualification incentives, contested jurisdiction and timing of alleged acts.
methodology.cadence: Daily: resolve procedural outcomes and assess material case or momentum developments; append a dated review even on holds. Reassess odds when material evidence warrants, otherwise hold explicitly. Weekly: compare all cases, discover omitted officials, challenge coalitions and momentum pathways, and review dated tests. No separate scheduled job.

cases.name: Pete Hegseth
cases.title: War powers and alleged operational abuses
cases.allegations: Eight articles allege war-powers violations and other abuses. Several concern the same Iran episode; article count is not independent evidence.
cases.defense: He rejects the effort as a policy disagreement. Presidential protection and shared responsibility for military decisions constrain a conviction coalition.
cases.watch: A completed House disposition, named senators’ positions and evidence addressing specific articles.

cases.name: Kristi Noem
cases.office: Former Homeland Security secretary; later State adviser
cases.title: Contracting and alleged false testimony
cases.allegations: Filed articles include self-dealing. A separate congressional referral alleges false testimony; neither establishes wrongdoing.
cases.defense: Noem defended the contracting process and described presidential approval. Contradictory accounts do not establish knowing deception or personal enrichment.
cases.watch: Contract records, responsibility and intent, final investigative findings and actual support for proceeding after departure.

cases.name: Kimberly Guilfoyle
cases.title: Alleged donor-access payments and gifts
cases.allegations: Oversight Democrats continue an inquiry after her departure into an alleged financial arrangement. Republican concern is not a conviction pledge.
cases.defense: Her lawyers describe unpaid prior professional fees and compliance with travel guidance. The central demand reportedly preceded confirmation, complicating an impeachment case.
cases.watch: Fee agreements, payment and communication records, in-office conduct and continued congressional action.

cases.name: Todd Blanche
cases.title: Alleged misuse of Justice Department authority
cases.allegations: House members have explicitly supported impeachment. Oversight may develop a case, but hypothetical future obstruction is not present misconduct.
cases.defense: Executive direction, official representation and disputed legal arguments are not by themselves proof of impeachable abuse.
cases.watch: Specific evidence of personal acts, court findings, congressional agenda and cross-party Senate support.

cases.name: Susie Wiles
cases.office: Former White House chief of staff
cases.title: Lobbying influence allegations
cases.allegations: Insider accusations and access relationships warrant tracing particular communications, decisions and benefits.
cases.defense: Lobbying relationships or a relative’s client do not themselves establish a corrupt exchange. Her particular position’s civil-officer eligibility needs resolution.
cases.watch: Specific personal acts, contrary evidence, congressional action and civil-officer eligibility.

pathways.assessment: Political punishment or public fatigue could discourage further impeachment and conviction votes.
